description:
Import an existing Gradle project into Eclipse, add a dependency, and implement a utility class.

Scenario: You have joined a team working on a data processing library. The source code is located at `/home/ga/projects/datautils` but is not yet imported into Eclipse.

Your task:
1. Import the existing Gradle project from `/home/ga/projects/datautils` into Eclipse (File > Import > Gradle > Existing Gradle Project).
2. Open `build.gradle` and add the Google Guava dependency to the `dependencies` block:
   `implementation 'com.google.guava:guava:33.0.0-jre'`
3. Refresh the Gradle project (Right-click project > Gradle > Refresh Gradle Project) to download the dependency.
4. Create a new Java class named `CollectionHelper` in the package `com.datautils.util` (src/main/java).
5. In `CollectionHelper.java`, implement the following methods using Guava's `ImmutableList` and `ImmutableMap`:
   - `public static <T> List<T> immutableListOf(T... elements)` returning `ImmutableList.copyOf(elements)`
   - `public static <K, V> Map<K, V> immutableMapOf(K k1, V v1, K k2, V v2)` returning `ImmutableMap.of(k1, v1, k2, v2)`
   - `public static <T> List<T> concat(List<T> first, List<T> second)` returning a list combined using `ImmutableList.builder()`
6. Build the project to ensure everything compiles successfully.
